catalysts.headline: Q3 2026 results: revenue $5.2M (+40.5% YoY from $3.7M), a secondary source frames this as a miss vs. a $6.21M consensus; net loss $61.2M (-$0.88/share GAAP per AP, described elsewhere as a beat vs. an $0.92 consensus or Zacks' -$0.84 average); R&D $35.5M (up from $34.4M YoY); SG&A $23.9M (+$4.5M YoY, mainly commercial-recruitment and IT costs); cash, cash equivalents and investment securities $768.4M as of 2026-09-30 (down from $810.3M at 2026-06-30), which the company says funds operations into 2030
FDA accepted uniQure's BLA for AMT-130 (Huntington's disease gene therapy) with Priority Review; secondary coverage reports a target PDUFA action date of 2027-05-01
catalysts.note: Secondary coverage states the PDUFA target date as May 1, 2027; flagged for independent primary-source confirmation given it is nearly 6 months past the Q3 2026 report date -- plausible given typical priority-review timelines (BLA accepted ~Nov 2026 + ~6 months), but the 8-K excerpt available this session did not itself state the date verbatim.

catalysts.headline: uniQure announced the FDA accepted its BLA for AMT-130 (ifezuntirgene inilparvovec, Huntington's disease gene therapy) under accelerated approval with Priority Review, with a confirmed PDUFA target action date of 2027-05-01 -- resolving the secondary-sourced-only date flagged in the prior pass. The FDA is tentatively planning an advisory committee meeting. uniQure and the FDA have agreed on the design of a confirmatory trial (~200 patients, randomized 2:1, primary endpoint at 36 months), with US patient screening expected to begin by year-end 2026. The UK MHRA has separately validated a parallel marketing authorization application. The filing relies on 36-month Phase 1/2 data vs. a propensity-score-matched external control from the Enroll-HD natural history database. This reverses the FDA's November 2025 position that the Phase 1/2 data were insufficient.
Barclays downgraded uniQure to Equal Weight from Overweight and cut its price target to $28 from $60
catalysts.impact: Shares reportedly opened lower the same day (from a $23.46 prior close to a $22.28 open per one secondary source); compounds pressure from the Sept 29 AMT-130 data readout

catalysts.headline: RBC Capital Markets maintained Outperform rating but cut price target from $65 to $48.
Shares partially recovered (+6.9% reported) the day after the Sept 29 selloff — this is a bounce, NOT the underlying catalyst.
Shares partly recovered, +6.9% to $26.21, as some analysts argued the prior day's selloff was overdone relative to price targets

AMT-130 (Huntington's disease gene therapy) four-year topline data showed the slowing of disease progression fall from ~80% at 3 years to ~44% at 4 years in the 12-patient high-dose cohort, missing statistical significance; uniQure said it still plans to pursue FDA approval based on the stronger 3-year data already submitted
catalysts.impact: Shares fell approximately 37% in a single session (reported variously as -37.14% to -37.3%); the following day (Sept 30) shares partially recovered +6.9% (already on file)

catalysts.headline: AMT-130 (Huntington's disease gene therapy) 48-month Phase I/II data update: Unified Huntington's Disease Rating Scale (UHDRS) showed 44% slowing of disease progression vs. updated external control — NOT statistically significant (p=0.144), down from a previously reported 75% slowing at 36 months. Shares fell ~37% (from ~$39.11 to ~$24.40). Company argued the 48-month readout understates the true effect due to missing data and dropout bias among faster-progressing external-control patients, and said 36-month data from 15 high-dose patients remains robust and underpins the planned BLA filing.

uniQure discloses additional 48-month AMT-130 Huntington's disease data: 80% slowing of disease progression (cUHDRS) at 36 months, but only 44% at 48 months (not statistically significant durability), alongside continued BLA priority-review process (submitted 2026-09-02)
catalysts.impact: Shares fell ~37% intraday/close from ~$39.11 to ~$24.51 on the session; subsequent shareholder securities-litigation investigation notices followed

catalysts.headline: uniQure submits Biologics License Application (BLA) to FDA for AMT-130 in Huntington's disease, requesting priority review; potential approval as soon as Q2 2027 if granted
catalysts.impact: Sets up the September data readout as a key event
